subject: general
question: At higher levels of development, which sector of the economy contributes less to the GDP?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Agriculture sector**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• At higher levels of development, the **Agriculture sector** contributes less to the GDP.
 
• As economies develop, there is a structural shift from agriculture to industrial and service sectors.
 
• In developed economies, the service sector typically becomes the dominant sector contributing to GDP.
 
• The industrial sector also plays a significant role in the GDP of developed countries, but the contribution from agriculture diminishes significantly.
 
• This shift reflects changes in productivity, labor force distribution, and economic priorities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The transition from an agriculture-based economy to one dominated by industry and services is known as **economic development**.
 
• Economic development is often accompanied by urbanization, improved infrastructure, and higher standards of living.
 
• Policies and investments in education, technology, and infrastructure are key drivers of this structural transformation.
 
• Despite its reduced share in GDP, the agriculture sector remains crucial for food security, employment, and rural development.
 
• Developed countries often have advanced agricultural practices that are highly efficient, contributing to a smaller but more productive agricultural sector.
